Test Description: Test MFA setup and validation process for high-privilege accounts
Specialized Test Steps:
1. Login as system administrator
2. Navigate to Security Settings → Multi-Factor Authentication
3. Test MFA Setup Process:
   - Generate QR code for Google Authenticator
   - Scan QR code with mobile authenticator app
   - Enter verification code from app
   - Save backup recovery codes
4. Logout and attempt login with MFA:
   - Enter username and password
   - System prompts for MFA code
   - Enter 6-digit code from authenticator app
   - Verify successful login with MFA badge
5. Test MFA Bypass Attempts:
   - Try login without MFA code
   - Test with expired MFA code (>30 seconds old)
   - Attempt login with incorrect MFA code
   - Test backup code usage
6. Test Account Lockout:
   - Enter wrong MFA code 5 times
   - Verify account locks for 15 minutes
   - Test admin unlock functionality
7. Test MFA Reset Process:
   - Request MFA reset via admin panel
   - Verify old MFA codes no longer work
   - Setup new MFA device and test
8. Test Session Behavior with MFA:
   - Verify MFA required only at login (not for each action)
   - Test session timeout with MFA-enabled account
   - Verify concurrent session limitations
Expected Result: MFA is properly implemented with secure setup process. Account lockout mechanisms work correctly. Session management respects MFA security levels.
Security Validation Points:
1. QR code generated with proper encoding and expiration
2. Authenticator app integration works with TOTP standard
3. Backup codes are cryptographically secure (12 codes, 8 chars each)
4. MFA bypass attempts fail with appropriate error messages
5. Account lockout triggers after 5 failed MFA attempts
6. Lockout duration is configurable (default 15 minutes)
7. Audit logs record all MFA events with timestamps
8. MFA reset requires admin approval and notification
9. Session cookies include MFA verification flag
10. Password change requires MFA re-verification
11. MFA settings cannot be disabled by user (admin only)
12. Backup codes can only be used once
Test Data Required:
Admin account with MFA capability
Google Authenticator or similar TOTP app
Test email account for notifications
Multiple devices for concurrent session testing
column19: Test with hardware tokens if available

Test Case Title: Password Policy Enforcement and Strength Testing
Test Description: Test comprehensive password policy implementation and strength validation
Specialized Test Steps:
1. Navigate to password change/registration form
2. Test Password Complexity Requirements:
   - Minimum 12 characters
   - At least 1 uppercase letter
   - At least 1 lowercase letter
   - At least 2 numbers
   - At least 1 special character (!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:,.<>?)
   - No dictionary words or common patterns
3. Test Password Strength Meter:
   - Enter weak password: 'password123' → Should show 'Weak'
   - Enter medium password: 'MyPass123!' → Should show 'Medium'
   - Enter strong password: 'R3h@b!1Ch@mp2024#Str0ng' → Should show 'Strong'
   - Test real-time strength indicator updates
4. Test Password History Prevention:
   - Change password to new strong password
   - Immediately try to change back to previous password
   - Verify system prevents reuse of last 12 passwords
   - Test password history across multiple changes
5. Test Common Password Prevention:
   - Try 'Password123!' → Should reject as too common
   - Try 'qwerty123!' → Should reject as keyboard pattern
   - Try '123456789!' → Should reject as numeric sequence
   - Try user's name + year → Should reject as personal info
6. Test Password Expiration Policy:
   - Set password expiration to 90 days for testing
   - Verify warning notifications start 14 days before expiration
   - Test forced password change on expiration
   - Verify expired account cannot login until password changed
7. Test Account Lockout for Failed Passwords:
   - Enter wrong password 5 times consecutively
   - Verify account locks for 30 minutes
   - Test progressive lockout (1min, 5min, 15min, 30min)
   - Verify lockout notification sent to user email
8. Test Password Reset Security:
   - Request password reset via email
   - Verify reset link expires in 1 hour
   - Test that reset link can only be used once
   - Verify old password is invalidated after reset
Expected Result: Password policy prevents weak passwords and enforces security standards. Account lockout mechanisms prevent brute force attacks. Password reset process is secure.
Security Validation Points:
1. Password complexity validation works in real-time
2. Strength meter accurately reflects password security
3. Common passwords database blocks 10,000+ weak passwords
4. Password history prevents reuse of last 12 passwords
5. Dictionary attack prevention works for English and local languages
6. Personal information (name, email, ID) cannot be used in password
7. Password expiration warnings sent at 14, 7, 3, 1 days before expiry
8. Expired passwords force immediate change on login
9. Account lockout triggers after 5 consecutive failed attempts
10. Progressive lockout increases duration: 1min → 5min → 15min → 30min
11. Password reset links expire in 60 minutes
12. Reset links are single-use and cryptographically secure
13. All password events logged with IP address and timestamp
Test Data Required:
Test accounts for password testing
Common password dictionary (rockyou.txt subset)
Email configuration for notifications
Various password combinations for testing
Notes: Test with password cracking tools if available

Test Description: Test comprehensive session security including hijacking prevention and concurrent session management
Specialized Test Steps:
1. Test Secure Session Creation:
   - Login with valid credentials
   - Inspect session cookie in browser dev tools
   - Verify cookie has HttpOnly flag (prevents XSS access)
   - Verify Secure flag is set (HTTPS only)
   - Verify SameSite attribute is set to 'Strict'
   - Check session ID is cryptographically random (128+ bits)
2. Test Session Fixation Prevention:
   - Note session ID before login
   - Complete login process
   - Verify session ID changes after authentication
   - Test that old session ID is invalidated
3. Test Session Hijacking Protection:
   - Login from Browser A and note session cookie
   - Open Browser B (different IP if possible)
   - Manually set same session cookie in Browser B
   - Attempt to access protected resources
   - Verify access denied due to IP/browser fingerprinting
4. Test Concurrent Session Management:
   - Login from Device 1 (Desktop Chrome)
   - Login from Device 2 (Mobile Safari) with same credentials
   - Test concurrent session policy:
     * Option A: Allow multiple sessions
     * Option B: Invalidate previous session
     * Option C: Prompt user to choose
   - Verify chosen policy is enforced correctly
5. Test Session Timeout Security:
   - Login and note session start time
   - Leave system idle for configured timeout (30 minutes)
   - Attempt to access protected resource
   - Verify automatic logout with security message
   - Test that session cannot be resumed
6. Test Session Invalidation:
   - Login and perform normal operations
   - Click logout button
   - Use browser back button to try accessing protected pages
   - Verify all pages redirect to login
   - Check that session cookie is properly cleared
7. Test Session Data Isolation:
   - Login as User A (Teacher role)
   - Note accessible menu items and data
   - Logout and login as User B (Admin role)
   - Verify no residual data from User A session
   - Test that role permissions are completely separate
8. Test Session Replay Attack Prevention:
   - Capture HTTP request with session cookie
   - Logout to invalidate session
   - Replay captured request
   - Verify request is rejected with 401 Unauthorized
Expected Result: Session management prevents hijacking and replay attacks. Concurrent sessions are properly managed. Session data isolation is complete between users.
Security Validation Points:
1. Session cookies have all security flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict
2. Session IDs are cryptographically random (minimum 128 bits entropy)
3. Session ID regenerates on authentication (prevents fixation)
4. IP address binding prevents session hijacking from different locations
5. Browser fingerprinting adds additional hijacking protection
6. Concurrent session policy enforced consistently
7. Session timeout configured appropriately (30 minutes idle)
8. Automatic logout warning appears 5 minutes before timeout
9. Session invalidation clears all server-side data
10. Logout invalidates session immediately and completely
11. Browser cache cannot access protected pages after logout
12. Session replay attacks fail with proper error messages
13. Cross-user session data never leaks between accounts
14. Role-based session data is completely isolated
Test Data Required:
Multiple user accounts with different roles
Multiple devices/browsers for concurrent testing
Network capture tools (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP)
Different IP addresses for hijacking tests

Test Description: Test comprehensive RBAC implementation including privilege escalation prevention
Specialized Test Steps:
1. Test Role Definition and Assignment:
   - Login as Admin and review role definitions
   - Verify roles: Admin, Teacher, Supervisor, AJK, Trainee
   - Check that each role has clearly defined permissions
   - Test role assignment process for new users
2. Test Admin Role Privileges:
   - Verify Admin can access all system functions
   - Test user management (create, edit, delete, role changes)
   - Test system configuration access
   - Test activity creation and modification
   - Test centre management capabilities
   - Verify Admin can view all centres' data
3. Test Teacher Role Restrictions:
   - Login as Teacher and test accessible functions
   - Verify can manage assigned activities only
   - Test attendance marking for own sessions only
   - Verify cannot access user management
   - Test cannot create new activities (Admin only)
   - Verify can view trainees enrolled in own activities only
4. Test Supervisor Role Capabilities:
   - Login as Supervisor and test oversight functions
   - Verify can view team performance reports
   - Test access to centre-specific data only
   - Verify cannot modify system settings
   - Test staff performance monitoring capabilities
   - Verify cannot access other centres' data
5. Test AJK Role Functionality:
   - Login as AJK and test facility management functions
   - Verify asset management capabilities
   - Test centre configuration access
   - Verify facility scheduling permissions
   - Test cannot access user personal data
   - Verify cannot modify activities or attendance
6. Test Trainee Role Limitations:
   - Login as Trainee and verify minimal access
   - Test can view own profile and schedule only
   - Verify cannot access other trainees' data
   - Test cannot modify any system data
   - Verify cannot access staff or admin functions
7. Test Privilege Escalation Prevention:
   - Attempt direct URL access to unauthorized pages
   - Test API endpoint access with insufficient privileges
   - Try to modify role through browser dev tools
   - Attempt SQL injection to elevate privileges
   - Test session token manipulation
8. Test Horizontal Privilege Escalation:
   - Login as Teacher A assigned to Centre 01
   - Attempt to access Centre 02 data
   - Try to view other teachers' sessions
   - Attempt to modify other teachers' data
   - Test trainee attempting to access other trainees' profiles
9. Test Dynamic Role Changes:
   - Admin changes Teacher role to Supervisor
   - Verify user must re-login for role change to take effect
   - Test that previous permissions are immediately revoked
   - Verify new permissions are properly applied
   - Test role change audit logging
Expected Result: RBAC system prevents unauthorized access completely. Privilege escalation attempts fail securely. Role changes are properly enforced with audit trails.
Security Validation Points:
1. Each role has clearly documented permissions matrix
2. Admin role has full system access without restrictions
3. Teacher role limited to assigned activities and enrolled trainees
4. Supervisor role limited to assigned centre data only
5. AJK role limited to facility and asset management
6. Trainee role limited to personal data viewing only
7. Direct URL access to unauthorized pages returns 403 Forbidden
8. API endpoints validate role permissions before processing
9. Browser dev tools cannot modify user roles or permissions
10. SQL injection attempts for privilege escalation fail
11. Session manipulation cannot elevate privileges
12. Cross-centre data access properly blocked
13. Role changes require admin privileges and user re-authentication
14. All access attempts logged with user, role, resource, and result
15. Unauthorized access attempts trigger security alerts
Test Data Required:
User accounts for each role type
Cross-centre test data for isolation testing
Security testing tools (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP)
Admin account for role management testing
